scope: Technical validation of 1,000 unpublished wave-five manuscripts and supporting repository integration; unresolved editorial flags remain explicit.

dataValidation.scope: Structural/provenance consistency and canonical publication gates. Community definitions are not OEM-verified diagnoses. Passing does not establish source accuracy, model applicability, deployment or indexing.

method.similarity: set Jaccard: intersection / union of all normalized five-word shingles
normalization: Remove frontmatter and all Markdown headings.
Stop before named source/applicability footer headings or Source/Reference/Citation/Scope/Applicability footer lines.
Remove code-directory links and URLs; retain other inline link labels.
Replace DTC identifiers and numeric literals with shared placeholders; lowercase and retain alphabetic tokens.
method.candidateRetrieval: Inverted index over shingles occurring in the configured document-frequency range. Count shared qualifying shingles only for pairs involving wave five; score candidates reaching the configured minimum (10 by default, less restrictive than the prior report's 25). No quadratic all-corpus pass.
method.exactDuplicateSupplement: SHA-256 equality of normalized bodies, including groups excluded by frequent-shingle filtering.
method.crossBatchSupplement: Also score the five prior-versus-wave-five and five different-wave-five-batch candidates with the most qualifying shared shingles. This bounded spot check can include pairs below the main candidate minimum.

limitations: This is a bounded lexical repetition screen, not an originality, plagiarism, source-accuracy, or factual-quality certification.
Candidate retrieval can miss pairs dominated by shingles appearing above the configured document-frequency ceiling or sharing fewer than the configured qualifying-shingle minimum.
Number and DTC normalization intentionally increases similarity among legitimate related factory procedures; scores require article-level review.
Paraphrased templates, semantic duplication, and copied source text not present in this corpus can evade lexical screening.
Footer removal uses an explicit heading list and footer-line patterns; inline applicability language remains when part of the main discussion.
The report is a point-in-time filesystem snapshot. A later manuscript change requires a rerun; stored reviews survive only identical normalized body hashes.
This is not a claim of production publication; the existing 4,000-article selection is unchanged.
180 of the 1,000 manuscripts retain unresolved source-review flags. Author source checks and bounded AI peer reviews do not certify every claim or repair outcome.
The 10,000-article overall campaign target remains unmet.
Static build checks do not verify live deployment, indexing, field performance or source factual accuracy.
